meta.title: Sofatap · Your iPhone, your living-room remote
meta.description: Sofatap turns your iPhone into a touchpad and a voice-and-text keyboard for the Windows, Mac or Linux computer connected to your TV. Open source.
nav.label: Main
lang.label: Language
hero.eyebrow: For the computer on your TV
hero.title: Your iPhone, your living‑room remote.
hero.lead: Sofatap turns your iPhone into a touchpad and a voice-and-text keyboard for the Windows, Mac or Linux computer connected to your TV. The picture stays on the big screen. You stay on the sofa.
hero.note: Open source · Windows, Mac and Linux
how.title: The whole screen is your touchpad
how.lead: One large rounded surface, with the logo, QR scanner, microphone and keyboard tucked inside its edges. A calm field of dots bends under your finger, and taps send out a ripple.
how.alt: The Sofatap iPhone screen: a dark rounded surface filled with small mint dots, the logo and a QR-scan icon at the top, and keyboard and microphone buttons at the bottom.
gesture.hold.result: Drag, until you lift your finger
how.note: The dots respond to your touch on the phone; they don’t show where the pointer is on the TV. With Reduce Motion on, the dots stay still.
type.title: Type without getting up
type.lead: Search for a film, fill in a form or reply to a message. Write it on the phone, check it, then send it to the computer.
type.step1.title: Tap the microphone
type.step1.body: It only listens after you tap it. When your iPhone and language support it, speech is recognized on the phone itself, and Sofatap doesn’t upload your audio.
type.step2.title: Check the draft
type.step2.body: Your words appear as an editable draft on the phone. You can also type with the iPhone keyboard or system dictation, or try a third-party keyboard such as Typeless (not fully tested yet). Those keyboards handle your data in their own way.
type.step3.title: Tap Send
type.step3.body: The text is typed into whichever field is focused on the computer. Sofatap doesn’t press Enter or submit anything for you.
type.keyboard: When a compatible computer reports that you’ve clicked into a text field, the phone keyboard can open on its own. This depends on the app exposing standard accessibility information, which not every app does, so the keyboard button is always there too.
setup.title: Set up once, then sit back
setup.step1.title: Install the computer app
setup.step1.body: Download the receiver for Windows, Mac or Linux. It opens a small window with a QR code.
setup.step2.title: Use the same home network
setup.step2.body: Connect the iPhone and computer to the same home network. Guest Wi-Fi that keeps devices apart may block the connection.
setup.step3.title: Scan the code and allow control
setup.step3.body: Open Sofatap on your iPhone and scan the code in the computer’s window. If the computer asks, allow Sofatap to control it, for example Accessibility on a Mac or the remote-control permission prompt on Linux with Wayland. Until then, pairing alone can’t move the pointer.
privacy.title: Stays in your home
privacy.network: Phone and computer talk directly over your home network, encrypted with TLS and a pinned certificate. There’s no relay server in between.
privacy.mic: The microphone turns on only when you tap it.
privacy.send: Nothing is typed on the computer until you tap Send.
privacy.code: The pairing code gives control of your computer, so keep it to yourself.
download.title: Get Sofatap
download.lead: Sofatap needs the iPhone app and a small receiver app on the computer. Both are early alpha software.
platform.iphone.source: Build the iPhone app from source
download.preview: These computer downloads are earlier alpha releases. The single-surface touch design, in-app voice input, automatic keyboard and refreshed receiver windows described on this page are in development and aren’t included yet.
platform.windows.name: Windows
platform.windows.note: Early alpha, not yet commercially code-signed. Extract the zip and run SofaTap.exe. Allow network access only on your trusted home network.
platform.mac.name: Mac
platform.mac.req: macOS 15 or later · Apple Silicon or Intel · Notarized by Apple
platform.mac.note: Alpha with limited testing so far. Pointer and text input on Intel Macs haven’t been tested yet.
platform.linux.name: Linux
platform.linux.req: x64 or ARM64 · GTK 3 · X11, with experimental Wayland
platform.linux.note: Alpha. Install the system packages listed in the setup guide first. X11 input has passed isolated desktop checks; Wayland support is experimental, and ARM64 hasn’t been run on real hardware yet.
faq.title: Questions
faq.screen.q: Do I see the computer’s screen on my phone?
faq.screen.a: No. The computer stays connected to your TV as usual, and you watch the big screen. Sofatap only sends pointer, scroll and text input from your phone.
faq.network.q: Does it work over Bluetooth or the internet?
faq.network.a: Neither. The phone and computer connect directly over your home network, so both need to be on the same network.
faq.enter.q: Will it press Enter or submit forms by itself?
faq.enter.a: No. Send types only the text you checked. Line breaks you write stay part of the text, but Sofatap never adds an Enter or a submit.
faq.keyboard.q: Does the keyboard pop up in every app?
faq.keyboard.a: Only for text fields that the app makes visible through accessibility information on a compatible receiver. Some apps, games and custom web widgets don’t, and on Linux this needs an optional accessibility component. You can always open the keyboard yourself.
faq.ready.q: Is Sofatap ready for everyday use?
faq.ready.a: Not yet. It’s an early alpha, and acceptance testing on real iPhones and computers is still pending. Expect rough edges, and please report problems on GitHub.
oss.title: Built in the open
oss.body: Sofatap is open source under the MIT license. Follow along, read the code or suggest improvements on GitHub.

demo.title: Try it: the phone moves the pointer on the TV
demo.hint: Move over the phone screen and the pointer moves on the TV. Click or tap once to select a film. Double-click or double-tap for a right click, then choose Play.
demo.keys: Keyboard: focus the phone screen, move the pointer with the arrow keys, press Enter to click and Shift+F10 or the Menu key to right-click. Escape closes the menu.
demo.tv: The TV shows a computer’s film library with nine films. The result of each gesture is announced in the status line.
demo.s.ready: Ready. The pointer is on the TV.
demo.s.clear: Left click on an empty area: nothing selected
demo.s.menuNone: Right click on an empty area. Point at a film to open its menu.
demo.s.demo: Demo playing. Touch the phone or press Stop to take over.
demo.s.done: Demo finished. Your turn: try it on the phone.
